equity_bridge.note: Q1-2026 balance sheet: non-current 1,560 + current 76; debt-like, deducted pre-tax (conservative)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr, rounded down; equity CAGR rejected (see warning)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 11.0% vs revenue 3.8% and EPS 5.6%: book value grew on low payout (~30%), FX/OCI and the 2021-22 COVID Life Science peak, not on underlying owner earnings. 3yr figures are all flat-to-negative (revenue -1.7%, EPS -7.8%, FCF -7.0%) as the bioprocessing destock, display/semis cycle and Healthcare patent expiries hit together. Selected 3.5% is revenue-based.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF equals reported FCF (SBC zero, interest income not stripped for a net-debt company), so the FCF CAGRs are on the owner basis. FCF CAGR (0.6% 5yr) far below revenue CAGR reflects rising capex (Life Science capacity build, 1.4bn FY21 -> 2.0-2.2bn FY23-25) and in-licensing upfronts inside intangible capex.

scenario_narratives.base: Life Science is the engine: bioprocessing demand normalises after the 2023-24 destock and grows mid-single-digit organically, lab/research steady despite US academic funding pressure. Electronics re-rates on AI-driven semiconductor materials (the FY26 guide implies +21-27% organic EBITDA pre) after the Surface Solutions exit, while displays drift. Healthcare shrinks in FY26 as Mavenclad goes generic in the US and Bavencio fades, then stabilises as SpringWorks' rare-tumour franchise (Ogsiveo, Gomekli) and fertility hold up. Group sales return to ~4% growth, reported EBITDA margin back to 28.5%, capex settles at ~D&A.
scenario_narratives.bull: Bioprocessing re-accelerates on biologics/ADC capacity and onshoring to the US; Electronics captures a larger share of advanced-node and HBM materials spend; Healthcare's pipeline (pimicotinib, SpringWorks assets, a successful in-licensed late-stage asset) more than replaces Mavenclad within three years. Mid-single-digit-plus growth and operating leverage take EBITDA margin to ~30.5%, near the 2021-22 peak, with capex easing to 9% of sales.
scenario_narratives.bear: Healthcare's patent cliff is deeper than replaced: Mavenclad erodes ex-US too, Bavencio declines, and the pipeline repeats the evobrutinib/xevinapant failures, so Merck pays up for more M&A at low returns (intangible capex stays at 10.5%). Bioprocessing recovery stalls on biotech funding and Chinese competition, the semis cycle turns, and tariffs/FX keep pressure on a Europe-cost/US-revenue base. Sales roughly flat for two years then ~2%, margin slides to 25.5%. Minority shareholders have no lever to change capital allocation under E. Merck KG control.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF of a diversified EUR-reporting science and technology group at a 7% EUR WACC, with all three segments in one consolidated flow (no SOTP: segment capex and tax are not separately disclosed in a way that supports a credible split). SBC-zero (cash-settled LTIP already in EBITDA), so house and street coincide. Risk is carried in the bear flows and a 25% bear weight, not in the discount rate.
key_risks_to_valuation: Healthcare loss of exclusivity (Mavenclad US from 2026, Bavencio) deeper or faster than the guide, with pipeline replacement failing
Bioprocessing recovery stalls; Life Science is the largest profit pool
Capital allocation under E. Merck KG control: further large acquisitions (SpringWorks ~3.9bn USD in 2025) at sub-WACC returns
EUR strength against USD/CNY on a European cost base (FY26 guide FX -3% to -1% on sales, -5% to -2% on EBITDA pre)
Year-one component FCF sits just above the 1.6-2.1bn company FCF guide; historical reported FCF has trailed the component bridge
Pending Bio-Techne acquisition (~EUR 9.9bn): excluded from this standalone model; overpayment or integration slippage would cut value per share, and net debt would roughly double on close

data_sources.qualitative: MRK.DE_Analysis.json (2026-10-25) plus outlook and segment sections of the FY2025 Annual Report and Q1-2026 Quarterly Statement

inputs.sbc_source: No equity-settled SBC: Merck's Long-Term Incentive Plan (Merck Share Units) is cash-settled, so its cost already sits in personnel expense inside EBITDA and in operating cash flow. FY2025 AR 'Share-based payments' line (3.8m) is immaterial. SBC-zero market: house and street coincide.
inputs.share_count_basis: 434,777,878 theoretical shares (FY2025 AR line 24754; unchanged since 2014): 129.2m listed shares plus E. Merck KG's equity interest expressed as share equivalents. Merck reports EPS on this basis and profit is shared pro rata (FY2025: dividends 284m to listed shareholders vs 755m profit withdrawal by E. Merck KG, the ~70% holder) so whole-group equity / 434.778m is the per-listed-share value. Held flat: no buybacks, no SBC dilution.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T15:35:21Z (Xetra regular session, last trade before the weekend)
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR-built. 10y Bund ~2.7% + ERP 5.0% x beta ~0.9 = cost of equity ~7.2-7.5%; pre-tax cost of debt ~3.5% (EUR bonds/hybrids), ~2.7% after tax; ~85/15 equity/debt at market value -> ~6.8%, rounded up to 7.0%. Same WACC in all scenarios: Healthcare patent cliff, pipeline and governance risk are charged in the bear flows and weights, not as a discount-rate premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: IFRS 16 lease liabilities (638m at 31-Mar-2026) are inside financial debt and therefore inside net_debt; lease principal is not deducted from the flows. Right-of-use renewals are small (~0.5% of sales) and are absorbed in the capex path.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI of 77m (31-Mar-2026) deducted once in the equity bridge; flows are consolidated. NCI share of profit is ~7-9m/yr, immaterial.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing row 'Operating company, non-US'): diversified operating company (Life Science ~43% of sales, Healthcare ~41%, Electronics ~16%), not a bank/REIT/holdco, so FCF is the right flow. NOT Merck & Co (MRK). Adaptations applied: EUR WACC; leases as debt (A); NCI in bridge; SBC-zero (band collapses, band_position null); risk charged once. NET DEBT = company's 'net financial debt' at 31-Mar-2026 (Q1-2026 statement line 323): financial debt 12,039 (bonds/CP 9,152, bank loans 190, liabilities to related parties i.e. E. Merck KG 1,967, other 65, derivatives 27, leases 638) less cash 2,743 and current financial assets 977 (cash field = 3,720 = both). Pension provisions (1,636) and NCI (77) are deducted in equity_bridge. Interest income NOT stripped: Merck is net-debt, interest received (65m FY2025) is small and net interest is negative. FY0 base: FY2025 revenue 21,102, reported EBITDA 5,899 (28.0%), D&A 2,298 incl. impairments, capex (PP&E + intangibles incl. in-licensing upfronts) 1,958, reported FCF 1,974 (OCF after interest and tax), cash taxes 939. FY2026 GUIDANCE (Q1-2026 statement, updated May 2026): sales 20.4-21.4bn (organic 0-3%, FX -3% to -1%, Surface Solutions divestiture ~-7% of Electronics), EBITDA pre 5.7-6.1bn, FCF 1.6-2.1bn, EPS pre 7.50-8.20; Healthcare organic -6% to -3% on Mavenclad US loss of exclusivity (dosing patents invalidated 30-Oct-2025). Component build calibration: the FY26 base path gives unlevered owner FCF ~2.5bn, i.e. ~2.25bn after ~0.25bn net interest, just above the top of the 1.6-2.1bn guide; historical reported FCF has run 0.1-0.8bn below an EBITDA-tax-interest-capex bridge (provisions, refund liabilities, working capital), which the negative wc_capture and front-loaded capex only partly capture -- the base is therefore not conservative on year one. GOVERNANCE: E. Merck KG (Merck family partnership) holds ~70% of total capital and controls the general partner; listed shareholders cannot change management or capital allocation. This is reflected in the bear weight and in using the theoretical share count (pro-rata economics), not in a WACC premium. VINTAGE: the H1-2026 interim (published Aug-2026) and Q3-2026 statement (due Nov-2026) are not yet extracted; balance sheet and guidance are from the Q1-2026 statement and should be refreshed when those land. PENDING M&A NOT MODELLED: Analysis.json (written in parallel, read after the first build) reports a pending Bio-Techne acquisition (~USD 11.3bn / EUR 9.9bn, announced June 2026, ~EUR 140m targeted synergies, close expected late 2026/early 2027) and the JSR chromatography purchase (closed March 2026, after the Q1 balance sheet). This valuation is STANDALONE: neither the deal's debt nor its cash flows are included. At a fair price a debt-funded deal is roughly value-neutral; at a typical life-science-tools premium it transfers value to Bio-Techne holders, which is part of why the bear weight is 25%. Rebuild with the acquired flows and ~EUR 10bn of added net debt once the deal closes.

base.growth_rationale: FY26 -1% = midpoint of 20.4-21.4bn guidance (organic +1.5%, FX -2%, Surface Solutions out). FY27-30 ~4%: Life Science organic +4-7% (bioprocessing recovery, Process Solutions) and Electronics AI-semis materials offset Healthcare's Mavenclad/Bavencio erosion, with SpringWorks (Ogsiveo, Gomekli) and pimicotinib as partial replacements. Fades to 2.5% by year 10.
base.margin_rationale: Reported-basis EBITDA (after ~0.1-0.2bn special items) below the 28.2% EBITDA-pre guide midpoint in FY26; recovers to 28.5%, inside the FY22-25 reported range of 26.1-29.3%.
base.capex_rationale: Capex incl. intangibles ran 9.3-10.3% of sales FY23-25; front-loaded at 10.5% for the Life Science build and recurring BD upfronts, then 9.5%, roughly equal to D&A ex-impairments (maintenance-plus).
base.tax_rationale: FY2025 cash taxes 939 / reported EBIT ~3,600 = 26%; underlying book rate guided at 22%; German statutory ~30%. 25% long-run cash rate.
base.wc_rationale: Manufacturer/distributor: receivables + inventories exceed payables, so growth consumes cash.
base.terminal_rationale: Cap 18x terminal owner FCF (~8.8x EV/EBITDA): below the 20x mature-compounder default because ~16% of sales (Electronics) is semiconductor/display-cyclical and Healthcare carries recurring patent-cliff risk; Gordon at 7%/2% is 20.4x so the cap binds. Bull 20x (default, Gordon 22x at 2.5%), bear 14x (Gordon 18.4x at 1.5%). All are below Merck's current ~12x EV/EBITDA, i.e. no multiple expansion assumed.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: Healthcare (~40% of sales) is mid patent cliff with a weak recent late-stage record, and the family-controlled KGaA structure leaves minority holders no recourse on capital allocation (e.g. further large M&A). Base 50%: the FY26 guide and Life Science/Electronics trends support it. Bull trimmed to 25% because it needs three independent things at once (bioprocessing upcycle, semis materials share gains, pipeline replacement of Mavenclad).
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
